title: WA Telecom Admin — Pretest C
description: 30-question NEC 2023 book-reference pretest with a 2-hour time allowance. Distribution: Introduction 2; General Requirements 3; Grounding and Bonding 3; Wiring Methods 3; Hazardous Locations 1; Special Conditions 4; Communications Systems 8; General Trade Knowledge and Theory 6. Code-based answers are drawn directly from the 2023 NEC text. Questions differ from Pretest B.

questions.question: When is unpowered equipment or an enclosure supplied by a coaxial cable considered grounded?
choices: When it is connected to the metallic cable shield
When it is mounted on a wooden surface
When the coaxial cable is longer than 15 m (50 ft)
When it is isolated from the cable shield
questions.answer: When it is connected to the metallic cable shield
questions.explanation: Unpowered equipment and enclosures, or equipment powered by the coaxial cable, are considered grounded when connected to the metallic cable shield. Reference: 820.103, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Two 100-ohm resistors are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
choices: 50 ohms
100 ohms
200 ohms
10,000 ohms
questions.answer: 50 ohms
questions.explanation: For two equal resistors in parallel, the equivalent resistance is one-half of either resistance: 100 / 2 = 50 ohms. Reference: General trade theory - parallel circuits.

questions.question: Which description matches the term "readily accessible"?
choices: Capable of being reached quickly without using tools other than keys, climbing over or under obstacles, removing obstacles, or using portable ladders
Capable of being reached only after removing part of the building finish
Visible from another piece of equipment and not more than 15 m (50 ft) away
Accessible only to qualified persons using special tools
questions.answer: Capable of being reached quickly without using tools other than keys, climbing over or under obstacles, removing obstacles, or using portable ladders
questions.explanation: This choice follows the Article 100 definition of Accessible, Readily (Readily Accessible). Reference: Article 100, Accessible, Readily, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What is the general rule for placing Class 2 or Class 3 conductors with electric light, power, Class 1, non-power-limited fire alarm, or medium-power network-powered broadband conductors?
choices: They must not be placed together in the same cable, cable tray, compartment, enclosure, manhole, box, raceway, or similar fitting unless specifically permitted
They must always be placed together to reduce installation cost
They may be placed together only when every conductor is smaller than 14 AWG
They may be placed together without restriction if the enclosure is metallic
questions.answer: They must not be placed together in the same cable, cable tray, compartment, enclosure, manhole, box, raceway, or similar fitting unless specifically permitted
questions.explanation: The general separation rule prohibits this mixing unless one of the specifically permitted conditions applies. Reference: 725.136(A), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: May a wiring system be installed in a duct used to transport dust, loose stock, or flammable vapors?
choices: No wiring system of any type may be installed in such a duct
Yes, if the circuit operates at 50 volts or less
Yes, if the conductors are Type THHN
Yes, if the wiring is supported every 1.8 m (6 ft)
questions.answer: No wiring system of any type may be installed in such a duct
questions.explanation: No wiring system of any type is permitted in ducts used to transport dust, loose stock, or flammable vapors. Reference: 300.22(A), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Which condition defines a Class I hazardous location?
choices: Flammable gases, flammable liquid-produced vapors, or combustible liquid-produced vapors are or may be present in the air in quantities sufficient to produce explosive or ignitible mixtures
Combustible dust is the only hazardous material present
Easily ignitible fibers or flyings are present but are not likely to be suspended in the air
Electrical equipment operates above 1000 volts in a dry room
questions.answer: Flammable gases, flammable liquid-produced vapors, or combustible liquid-produced vapors are or may be present in the air in quantities sufficient to produce explosive or ignitible mixtures
questions.explanation: This is the Code description of a Class I location. Reference: 500.5(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Which optical fiber cable types are permitted to be installed directly in a space used for environmental air?
choices: Types OFNP and OFCP
Types OFNR and OFCR only
Types OFNG and OFCG only
Types OFN and OFC only
questions.answer: Types OFNP and OFCP
questions.explanation: Types OFNP and OFCP are the optical fiber cable types permitted directly in other spaces used for environmental air. Reference: 770.113(C)(1), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: A 48-volt source is connected across a 12-ohm load. What current flows through the load?
choices: 4 amperes
0.25 ampere
36 amperes
576 amperes
questions.answer: 4 amperes
questions.explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V / R = 48 / 12 = 4 amperes. Reference: General trade theory - Ohm's law.

questions.question: A device operates at 24 volts and draws 2 amperes. How much power does it consume?
choices: 48 watts
12 watts
22 watts
96 watts
questions.answer: 48 watts
questions.explanation: Electrical power is P = V × I = 24 × 2 = 48 watts. Reference: General trade theory - electric power.

questions.question: What is the maximum permitted length of qualifying unlisted outside-plant communications or CATV-type coaxial cable inside a building, measured from its point of entrance?
questions.explanation: Qualifying unlisted outside-plant cable may extend no more than 15 m (50 ft) inside the building from its point of entrance. Reference: 800.48(1), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: How must equipment that is listed, labeled, or identified for a use be installed and used?
choices: In accordance with any instructions included in the listing, labeling, or identification
Only in accordance with the installer's customary practice
Without regard to instructions if the equipment operates normally
Only after its listing mark has been removed
questions.answer: In accordance with any instructions included in the listing, labeling, or identification
questions.explanation: Listed, labeled, or identified equipment must be installed and used in accordance with instructions included in its listing, labeling, or identification. Reference: 110.3(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Are informational notes enforceable as Code requirements?
choices: No, informational notes are informational only and are not enforceable as Code requirements
Yes, every informational note is a mandatory rule
Yes, but only when an installer chooses to follow it
No, because informational notes are product warranties
questions.answer: No, informational notes are informational only and are not enforceable as Code requirements
questions.explanation: The explanatory-material rule states that informational notes are informational only and are not enforceable as requirements of the Code. Reference: 90.5(C), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: How is the interior of an underground enclosure or raceway classified?
choices: As a wet location
As a dry location
As a damp location only
As an unclassified location regardless of moisture
questions.answer: As a wet location
questions.explanation: The interior of enclosures or raceways installed underground is considered a wet location. Reference: 300.5(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Which method is permitted for splicing a wire-type grounding electrode conductor?
choices: An irreversible compression-type connector listed as grounding and bonding equipment
A removable twist-on wire connector
An unlisted split-bolt wrapped only with tape
A soldered lap joint without mechanical connection
questions.answer: An irreversible compression-type connector listed as grounding and bonding equipment
questions.explanation: A wire-type grounding electrode conductor may be spliced using an irreversible compression-type connector listed as grounding and bonding equipment; exothermic welding is also permitted. Reference: 250.64(C)(1), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What is the minimum size of a communications bonding conductor or grounding electrode conductor?
choices: 14 AWG
18 AWG
10 AWG
6 AWG
questions.answer: 14 AWG
questions.explanation: The communications bonding conductor or grounding electrode conductor must not be smaller than 14 AWG and is not required to exceed 6 AWG. Reference: 800.100(A)(3), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What other loads may the branch circuit supplying non-power-limited fire alarm equipment supply?
choices: No other loads
Any lighting load on the same floor
Only receptacle loads rated 15 amperes or less
Only communications equipment loads
questions.answer: No other loads
questions.explanation: The branch circuit supplying non-power-limited fire alarm equipment must supply no other loads. Reference: 760.41(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: How must an unused opening in electrical equipment generally be closed?
choices: To afford protection substantially equivalent to the wall of the equipment
With any combustible material available at the job site
Only enough to prevent the entry of visible light
It may remain open if the equipment is indoors
questions.answer: To afford protection substantially equivalent to the wall of the equipment
questions.explanation: Unused openings, other than the stated permitted openings, must be closed to afford protection substantially equivalent to the equipment wall. Reference: 110.12(A), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What must be done with all grounding electrodes described by the Code that are present at a building or structure served?
choices: They must be bonded together to form the grounding electrode system
Only the electrode closest to the service may be used
They must remain electrically isolated from one another
They may be omitted whenever a metal water pipe is present
questions.answer: They must be bonded together to form the grounding electrode system
questions.explanation: All qualifying grounding electrodes present at the building or structure must be bonded together to form the grounding electrode system. Reference: 250.50, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What separation is generally required between communications or CATV-type coaxial cables and conductors of electric light, power, Class 1, non-power-limited fire alarm, or medium-power network-powered broadband circuits in other applications?
choices: At least 50 mm (2 in.)
At least 6 mm (1/4 in.)
At least 300 mm (12 in.)
At least 1.8 m (6 ft)
questions.answer: At least 50 mm (2 in.)
questions.explanation: The general separation for these other applications is at least 50 mm (2 in.), subject to the stated exceptions. Reference: 800.133(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: May an outdoor antenna or its lead-in conductor be attached to an electric service mast?
choices: No, neither may be attached to the electric service mast
Yes, if the antenna is receiving only
Yes, if the mast is bonded
Yes, if the attachment is at least 3 m (10 ft) above grade
questions.answer: No, neither may be attached to the electric service mast
questions.explanation: Outdoor antennas and lead-in conductors must be securely supported and must not be attached to the electric service mast. Reference: 810.12, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: A signal amplifier provides a power gain of 10 dB. What is the output-to-input power ratio?
choices: 10 to 1
2 to 1
20 to 1
questions.answer: 10 to 1
questions.explanation: For power, dB = 10 log10(Pout / Pin). Therefore, a 10 dB gain corresponds to a power ratio of 10 to 1. Reference: General trade theory - decibels.

questions.question: Eight 75-watt devices operate continuously for 10 hours. How much electrical energy do they use?
choices: 6 kilowatt-hours
0.6 kilowatt-hour
60 kilowatt-hours
600 kilowatt-hours
questions.answer: 6 kilowatt-hours
questions.explanation: Total power is 8 × 75 = 600 watts, or 0.6 kilowatt. Energy is 0.6 kW × 10 h = 6 kWh. Reference: General trade theory - electrical energy.

questions.question: Which cable types are required for low-power network-powered broadband communications circuits located outside and entering buildings?
choices: Type BLU or Type BLX
Type BMU or Type BMR only
Type OFNP or Type OFCP
Type CL2P or Type CL3P
questions.answer: Type BLU or Type BLX
questions.explanation: Low-power network-powered broadband circuits located outside and entering buildings must use Type BLU or Type BLX cable, subject to permitted substitutions. Reference: 830.40(B), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: How must a ferrous metal raceway enclosing a grounding electrode conductor be bonded?
choices: At each end of the raceway or enclosure
At the grounding electrode end only
At the equipment end only
Bonding is not required for ferrous metal raceways
questions.answer: At each end of the raceway or enclosure
questions.explanation: Ferrous metal raceways, enclosures, and cable armor for grounding electrode conductors must be bonded at each end to create an electrically parallel path. Reference: 250.64(E)(1), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: When cable or a raceway-type wiring method passes through bored holes in wood framing, what minimum distance is generally required between the edge of the hole and the edge of the wood member?
choices: 50 mm (2 in.)
questions.explanation: Bored holes must generally be located so their edge is not less than 32 mm (1 1/4 in.) from the edge of the wood member. Reference: 300.4(A)(1), 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What must be done with the accessible portion of abandoned Class 4 cable?
choices: It must be removed
It must be energized and left in place
It must be painted orange
It must be connected to the nearest grounding electrode
questions.answer: It must be removed
questions.explanation: The accessible portion of abandoned cables must be removed; a cable identified for future use is not abandoned. Reference: 722.25, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: What listing characteristic is required for cable ties intended for use in spaces used for environmental air?
choices: Low smoke and heat release properties
Oil resistance only
Direct-burial suitability only
Sunlight resistance only
questions.answer: Low smoke and heat release properties
questions.explanation: Cable ties intended for use in environmental-air spaces must be listed as having low smoke and heat release properties. Reference: 800.170, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: For new dwelling construction, what minimum communications outlet installation is required?
choices: At least one communications outlet in a readily accessible area, cabled to the service provider demarcation point
One communications outlet in every room, with no demarcation-point cable
One outlet outdoors only
No communications outlet is required in new construction
questions.answer: At least one communications outlet in a readily accessible area, cabled to the service provider demarcation point
questions.explanation: New construction requires a minimum of one communications outlet within the dwelling in a readily accessible area and cabled to the service provider demarcation point. Reference: 805.156, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: How do the requirements for communications systems relate to the requirements in Chapters 1 through 7?
choices: They are not subject to Chapters 1 through 7 except where those requirements are specifically referenced in Chapter 8
They are subject to every requirement in Chapters 1 through 7 without exception
They replace Chapters 1 through 7 for all electrical installations
They are informational only and contain no enforceable requirements
questions.answer: They are not subject to Chapters 1 through 7 except where those requirements are specifically referenced in Chapter 8
questions.explanation: Chapter 8 covers communications systems and is not subject to Chapters 1 through 7 except where their requirements are specifically referenced in Chapter 8. Reference: 90.3, 2023 NEC.

questions.question: Three resistors of 120 ohms, 330 ohms, and 550 ohms are connected in series. What is their total resistance?
choices: 1000 ohms
333.3 ohms
45.5 ohms
questions.answer: 1000 ohms
questions.explanation: Series resistances add: 120 + 330 + 550 = 1000 ohms. Reference: General trade theory - series circuits.
